newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy judge adjourns Prodi hearing til June 30.
newsitem.headline: Italy judge adjourns Prodi hearing til June 30.

text.p: A judge who must decide whether to put Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi on trial appointed a panel of experts on Wednesday to examine financial aspects of the case and gave them at least 90 days to complete their work.

Committal judge Edoardo Landi named five experts in accounting, commercial law and management to carry out the study into a controversial privatisation in 1993 at the root of allegations of abuse of office.

Prodi, head of a centre-left government since last May, was chairman of giant state industrial holding IRI in October 1993 when it sold food group Cirio to a little-known southern consortium, Fis.Vi for 310 billion lire ($184 million).
Public prosecutor Giuseppa Geremia alleges that Prodi and five other IRI board members at the time awarded an "unjust advantage" to Fis.Vi.
Geremia has asked the court to indict Prodi and the other five on a charge of abuse of office. All deny the allegations.
Landi agreed to a request from the experts for 90 days to complete their study, with the option of an extension if they require more time. He set the next hearing for June 30.

The judge agreed to appoint the panel at the previous hearing on February 28 in response to a petition from one of the former IRI board members, Mario Draghi, who is now director general of the Treasury Ministry.
Prodi has said he will not resign even if the case is sent to trial. He has suffered no evident political damage from the case, which does not involve any allegations of personal enrichment.
